title: Intent from Homebrew on Linux and macOS, with no source checkout: Linux binaries on every release
objective:
A developer installs Intent with Homebrew on Linux or macOS and has a working Intent with no checkout of Intent's source tree: the CLI, the daemon, the hooks and skills, and the pre-commit gate. Every release tag on GitHub carries Linux packages built by GitHub Actions beside the macOS assets, and the tap's formula installs the one that fits the machine. Windows is reached through WSL, which is ST0082's, built on this thread; there is no native Windows port.

Concretely:

1. A release workflow builds `intent` and `intentd` for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux, and packages them with the support payload the binaries read at run time, so a download installs rather than being a bare binary.
2. The binaries run on Linux distributions older than the build host: they are linked statically against musl, and the workflow proves it by running them in a container at an old floor.
3. A `workflow_dispatch` run builds the same packages without a tag, so a tag is never the workflow's first run.
4. The Linux packages reach each tag's GitHub release with one writer per release object, so nothing in CI races the local release flow's `gh release create`.
5. The formula in `matthewsinclair/homebrew-intent` carries Linux entries for both architectures beside the macOS one, written by the release tooling, so `brew install` works on Linux as it does on macOS.
6. Intent installed from its Linux package works on Ubuntu as a user uses it, proven on hv's Ubuntu VM, whose coreutils are uutils and whose awk is mawk.
7. The docs carry Intent's Linux install through Homebrew.
8. `intent daemon start --at-login` and `intent daemon stop --at-login` refuse on Linux before they write anything.

As built, measured 2026-10-12 on main a581c15c7 and on GitHub's v3.2.3:

- `bin/devbin release check` warns on any workflow that has a `tags:` trigger and calls `gh release`, an upload included (`check_release_writers` in `bin/.devbin/lib/cmd/release`: one writer per release object). devbin is vendored here, so a change to its release steps is the Devbin project's to make.

Measured 2026-10-14 on main 72732afb4:

Separate from this thread, and outside Intent's tree: the other estate mirrors GitHub's tags (v3.2.3 and later) and main to its own server from a bare clone of GitHub outside every Intent checkout, and each sync starts on vc's word that a release is tagged. hv ruled on 2026-10-12, through that estate's dc node, that its server also hosts each release's binaries beside the tag, starting with the first release that ships Linux binaries (3.2.4 if this thread lands in it), while v3.2.3 stays tag-only. hv's rulings in vc's session, 2026-10-12, that stay with this thread: it rides Intent 3.2.4, built by cc after the 3.2.4 CHANGELOG section; WP-01's dispatch run goes first, because it produces the packages devbin's joint check installs; and `intent daemon start --at-login` refuses on Linux before it writes anything (WP-05). Linux proving, hv's rulings of 2026-10-12 given to devbin-vc and relayed: the tests run on hv's Ubuntu VM before anything is pushed, nothing goes to GitHub until it works there, and there is one release, 3.2.4, cut only once the work runs on main's HEAD, with no run of releases in quick succession. wps.title: Linux release binaries built by GitHub Actions
wps.objective: A workflow builds `intent` and `intentd` for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux, statically or against an old glibc floor because the distributions they will run on are not known, packages them with the support payload the binaries read at run time, runs the packaged `intent --version` inside a container at that floor, and keeps each package as a workflow artifact. It runs on `workflow_dispatch`, so it is proven before any tag runs it. Its first measurement is whether `intent-support.tar.gz` serves Linux unchanged. aarch64 became required on 2026-10-14, because Homebrew on Linux is proven first on hv's aarch64 VM.

wps.title: Linux assets on each tag's GitHub release, one writer per release object
wps.objective: Each release tag's GitHub release carries the Linux assets beside the macOS ones, with one writer per release object. `bin/devbin release check` warns on a workflow that has a `tags:` trigger and calls `gh release`, an upload included, so there are two candidate shapes: the local release flow downloads the workflow's artifacts and uploads them after it creates the release, which changes devbin and so is the Devbin project's to build; or a workflow with no `tags:` trigger, dispatched once the release exists, uploads to it and never creates one. The chosen shape is written into `intent/docs/releasing.md`, and `bin/devbin release check` names no second writer.

wps.title: Intent's Linux install through Homebrew, in docs/install.md
wps.objective: `docs/install.md` carries Intent's Linux install in a bare `## Linux` section, so its anchor is `#linux`: Homebrew on Linux, then `brew install matthewsinclair/intent/intent`, `intent bootstrap` and `intent doctor`, with no checkout of Intent's source tree. It is the install step's one home: ST0082's WSL page links to it and never restates it, and devbin's README points at it. The page's sections on verifying an install and on what an install has to contain read true for the Linux package, by a line or by a pointer. Every command on the page is run on Linux before it is written down: drafted from hv's Ubuntu VM, and run again from the tap once a release carries the Linux packages. Whether devbin also installs Intent is the Devbin project's call; this install is needed either way. The WSL page this package also held moved to ST0082 on 2026-10-14. Its bank also carries this thread's two lines in the release's CHANGELOG section, one for the Linux packages and the Homebrew install on Linux and one for WP-05's `--at-login` refusal (vc under hv's pen, 2026-10-13, carried here 2026-10-14).

wps.objective: A developer installs Intent from a tagged release under WSL on a real Windows machine by following the docs, and reports `intent --version`, `intent doctor`, and one thread created and listed in a project in the WSL filesystem. hv arranges the run through the other estate; Intent's nodes cannot run it.

wps.title: intent daemon start --at-login refuses on Linux before writing anything
wps.objective: On a machine without launchd, `intent daemon start --at-login` refuses before it writes anything, so no `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` plist appears on Linux, and its remedy names `intent daemon start` without the flag as the way to run the daemon. `intent daemon stop --at-login` refuses the same way. Today `daemon_start` in `intent-cli/src/render.rs` writes the plist through `launchagent::write_plist` and only then fails at `launchctl`, whose `NoLaunchctl` remedy in `intentsvcs/src/launchagent.rs` already says the right thing; the refusal moves ahead of the write. Linux CI runs the test that proves it.

wps.title: The Homebrew formula installs Intent on Linux
wps.objective: The formula the release tooling writes for `matthewsinclair/homebrew-intent` carries Linux entries for x86_64 and aarch64 beside the macOS one, each pointing at that release's Linux package, so `brew install matthewsinclair/intent/intent` works on Linux with no source checkout, as it does on macOS. The 3.2.3 formula declares `depends_on :macos` and arm64, by hv's ruling of 2026-08-15, which hv widened to Linux on 2026-10-14. Until a release carries Linux packages, the formula is rehearsed on hv's Ubuntu VM from a local copy against the package the VM built. The install from the tap is proven once the first release with Linux packages is published, and the macOS install is re-proven on a Mac with no checkout when hv loops back to it. Shape agreed on 2026-10-14 (cc's proposal, vc's yes under hv's pen): the formula writer, and smoke beside it, move out of `cmd/macos` to one home both release steps call. `on_linux` entries for each architecture override the top-level url, which stays macOS arm64's because `brew tap` validates every simulated platform. `depends_on :macos` goes, and `arch: :arm64` moves inside `on_macos` with the intentd and support resources. The Linux branch installs the unpacked package into libexec and shares the chmod and symlink tail. Every sha256 is read from the bytes the release serves. A dev-tap input of base URL plus hashes lets hv's Ubuntu VM prove the formula from file:// URLs before any push. publish asks for its own assets by name instead of refusing any release that already carries assets, and its notes stop saying macOS-only.

wps.title: Intent on Ubuntu from its Linux package, as a user uses it
wps.objective: Intent installed from its Linux package, with no checkout of Intent's source, works on Ubuntu as a user uses it, proven on hv's Ubuntu VM, whose coreutils are uutils and whose awk is mawk. The drive covers `intent --version` and `intent bootstrap`; a new project in which `intent doctor` reports no finding; the thread, work package and acceptance verbs; the whiteboard; the daemon started and stopped without `--at-login`, and the `--at-login` refusal; `intent claude upgrade --apply`, with its hooks firing in a Claude Code session; and the critic gate with shellcheck on PATH. Intent's shell suite runs once on the same host, because uutils and mawk are what Ubuntu 26.04 ships. Every step runs as a bash script with its log, never as commands typed into an agent's own shell, whose `grep` and `find` are wrappers. Each defect found is filed as an issue and fixed before the push, and the drive runs again on the commit that is pushed.
